correctness.rationale: On the real unweighted edge-coordinate ell1 space of a uniformly r-subdivided K_n, n>=3,r>=1, internal degree-2 conservation forces circulations constant on each subdivided base edge, Z_{n,r}=RZ_0. For the complete-graph projection P_0=I-B^T(BB^T)^+B, antisymmetric formula subtracts (s_i-s_j)/n and each absolute column sum L=3(n-2)/n. S_n covariance and a fixed-edge stabilizer show that all invariant circulation projections are parameterized by symmetric path-layer weights w with sum1. Their ell1 norm rL max|w_t| minimizes uniquely at w_t=1/r. The transpose-complement correspondence for cut projections makes each relevant row norm |1-dw_t|+L||w||_1-d|w_t|; choosing a layer weight <=1/r proves >=1+L-2d/r, with equality for uniform weights. Averaging arbitrary projections over the finite signed-isometry group proves global optimality without assuming equivariance. The formulas and n>=5 order-reversal on r=1 versus r>=2 follow. Uniqueness is asserted only among invariant minimizers, not all minimizers.

value.rationale: Determines two natural relative Banach-space projection invariants on an infinite family of subdivided complete graphs, including exact cut-versus-cycle order reversal as edge paths lengthen. The proof supplies an explicit globally optimal projector over all competitors, and the r=1 and n=3 reductions give meaningful checks rather than arbitrary parameter slicing.

limitations: An unlocated representation-theoretic graph projection classification could contain equivalent formulas under cocycle/flow terminology.
For r=1, some complete graph projection constants are classical; novelty is the coupled r-family and strict reversal, not each boundary value.
Prior papers are not treated as mathematical proof or external certification. Finite reproductions do not establish infinite parameter families.
